question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Washout time-course of AP-1 occupancy and accessibility
ideas.description: After a transient stimulus, profile FOS/JUN CUT&RUN and ATAC footprinting at multiple times post-washout to see whether AP-1 binding and open chromatin persist beyond signaling and TF protein levels. Persistent sites that predict faster secondary transcription define candidate memory loci.

ideas.title: Stage-specific acute degradation (degron) of AP-1
ideas.description: Use dTAG/AID-tagged JUN/FOS to deplete AP-1 only during priming, only during the memory (washout) interval, or only at rechallenge, then measure the secondary response. This separates AP-1 as the initiator from AP-1 as the maintainer of memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage/sister-cell tracking
ideas.description: Combine live imaging of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN with sister-cell tracking and post-hoc multiome to test whether AP-1 state and accessibility are inherited across divisions and predict each cell's re-response. Mitotic retention can be checked simultaneously.

ideas.title: Hysteresis and optogenetic dose-duration mapping
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 with optogenetic or titratable inputs across ramp-up and ramp-down sweeps and varied pulse patterns, then measure output. Path-dependent output (hysteresis) or persistent state would indicate feedback-based memory.

ideas.title: Locus-specific motif editing and dCas9 perturbation
ideas.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers, or recruit AP-1 or dominant-negative A-FOS with dCas9, and test primed re-response by RNA and accessibility. Loss or gain of memory at single loci tests necessity and sufficiency independent of global AP-1 changes.

candidates: Time-course ChIP/CUT&RUN of AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy before, during, and after a transient stimulus
ATAC-seq footprinting of AP-1 motifs after stimulus washout to track persistent accessibility
Acute degron (dTAG/AID) depletion of JUN/FOS after stimulus to test maintenance vs. initiation of memory
Optogenetic pulse-controlled AP-1 activation with varied dose/duration followed by re-challenge
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) of primed vs naive cells to link AP-1 motif accessibility to secondary response
Live imaging of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN to measure single-cell dynamics and inheritance across divisions
Sister-cell lineage tracking to test heritability of AP-1 state through mitosis
Mitotic bookmarking assay: AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes by live imaging/CUT&RUN
Dominant-negative (A-FOS) induction only during priming vs only during rechallenge
Targeted dCas9 recruitment of AP-1 or its antagonist to specific enhancers to test sufficiency of memory sites
Mutating AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers by CRISPR base editing
Hi-C/Micro-C to measure AP-1-dependent loop persistence after stimulus
Histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) to test whether AP-1 sites leave chromatin scars independent of AP-1
Test BAF/SWI-SNF dependence of persistent AP-1 sites via inhibitors during washout
Mathematical modeling of FOS/JUN positive feedback bistability and hysteresis predictions
Dose-response hysteresis measurement: sweep stimulus up and down and compare thresholds
Compare AP-1 family member switching (FOSL1/FOSL2/JUNB) composition over time by proteomics
In vivo models: epithelial wound-healing or inflammatory memory with AP-1 conditional knockout
Phosphorylation/JNK-signaling reporter plus AP-1 occupancy to separate signaling memory from chromatin memory
Cross-cell-type comparison of AP-1 memory in human fibroblast reprogramming or senescence contexts
